$comment: The manifest digest every PUBLISHED connector tag put on the registry,
with the immutable coordinates that prove the publication. Measured by
`scripts/released_manifest_sweep.py`, guarded by
`tests/architecture/test_released_manifest_digests.py`.
## Why this file exists at all
An installation adopts a connector by MANIFEST DIGEST. `mod_intg` stores
the digest a binding was enabled against, and
`dotmac_integration.spi.accepts_manifest_digest` answers 'is this
installation still adoptable?' by asking whether the plugin still carries
a manifest with that digest.
Nothing stopped a change from editing the manifest of an ALREADY-PUBLISHED
version. Do that and one version name means two contracts: the wheel on
the registry published digest A, the repository publishes digest B under
the same version string, and an installation adopted against A becomes
unidentifiable — `accepts_manifest_digest` returns False for a digest the
connector really did publish.
It was not theoretical. Five connectors reached this file's first commit
declaring their published version while carrying a different manifest, and
two of them — flutterwave and remita — carried TWO manifests both claiming
the same version string. Every existing gate was green: the
version-identity guard compares three version SURFACES, the publication
sweep compares a version to a TAG, and neither reads a manifest.
## Why a checked-in ledger rather than deriving from the tags
Deriving is possible and is exactly how every digest below was produced
(`--verify-tags`). It is not admissible as THE gate, for the reason
`declared-publication-baseline.json` already gives about querying the
index: a gate that cannot run is not a gate.
* Deriving needs TAGS. `actions/checkout` fetches none by default, so on
the cheap `quality` matrix every pull request runs, a derived check
would refuse on every run — and refusing-as-passing is how
`test_declared_publication.py` spent its life green while checking
nothing.
* Deriving needs to IMPORT code from an arbitrary older revision against
today's SPI. That works for all eleven connector tags today, and it is
the kind of thing that stops working silently.
* A digest in a file is REVIEWABLE. An edit to a published manifest shows
up in the diff as a digest change beside the capability list that
produced it, while somebody can still object.
So the ledger is the primary and it runs offline with no git at all:
`--check` reads this file and the working tree, nothing else. The
derivation is the CROSS-CHECK, which is what stops the ledger being
brought into line with a bad edit in one commit — doctoring it then
requires moving a tag on `origin`. Same two-half shape
`test_released_migrations.py` uses for released migration BYTES, applied
to the published CONTRACT.
## What a row is, and what it is not
A row is a positive, permanent, oracle-backed fact (AGENTS.md rule 30):
this distribution published this version, the tag peels to this commit,
and the manifest that tag declares hashes to this digest. Positive claims
do not expire, so unlike `declared-publication-baseline.json` this ledger
only GROWS — a row is never removed because a version got old. Removing
one is removing the record of something consumers still hold.
`release_run` is recorded where the repository can still name it (the
changelog entry written at release time). Four of the eleven tags predate
that habit and carry an empty string rather than a guess; `peeled_commit`
is the oracle actually relied on in every case, and an empty
`release_run` is an absent second coordinate, never a weaker claim.
## The digest is measured, not transcribed
Both sides of every comparison are computed by `ConnectorManifest.digest`,
the ONE owner of the contract-identity rule. This file therefore does not
claim to reproduce the hash function that ran in August 2026 — it records
what today's SPI computes for the manifest each TAG declares, which is
what makes the comparison meaningful: a difference is a difference in the
contract rather than in the arithmetic. A change to the digest formula
itself moves every row at once, which is the correct signal, because it
moves every installation's pin at once.
## Scope
Connector distributions listed in `.github/release-connectors.json`, which
owns their coordinates (import name, plugin attribute, tag prefix) and is
read rather than copied. Installable MODULES are UNMONITORED here rather
than exempt (ADR-0018): `ModuleManifest` exposes no digest and no
installation adopts a module by one — a module's published bytes are held
immutable by `test_released_migrations.py` instead.
`test_the_unmonitored_distributions_are_named` lists them.
